title: Quantized-timer skew caused intermittent batch voids and fairness drift — remediation plan
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-18 we observed intermittent "void" windows where the continuous coalescer produced zero formed batches for short intervals (~200-800ms) on a subset of shards. The symptom was a correlated tail-latency spike for small, latency-sensitive requests and a slow drift in per-tenant success rates (fairness skew). This ticket captures investigation findings, mitigations applied during the incident, and the longer-term fixes and verification plan.
impact: Approximately 4% of production requests experienced tail-latency > 500ms across two clusters for ~45 minutes; customer-visible errors were low but latency-sensitive features degraded (chat turn latency and small-completion endpoints). Customer impact: medium.
timeline:
- 2026-02-18 11:03 UTC: Alerting flagged tail-latency increase on service 'inference-coalescer'.
- 2026-02-18 11:06 UTC: Pager acknowledged; rotating on-call ran initial dashboard queries (p50/p95/p99, batch formation rate).
- 2026-02-18 11:12 UTC: Identified repeated short windows with zero formed batches; KV cache metrics unchanged.
- 2026-02-18 11:25 UTC: Temporary mitigation: disable tenant-ribbon affinity batching heuristic for impacted shard pool. Latency trend improved within 7 minutes.
- 2026-02-20: Deeper investigation started to reproduce and root cause.
root_cause: A previously unnoticed interaction between the quantized timer wheel used for window coalescence and tenant-level ribbon routing caused aligned timer ticks to skip forming windows in edge alignment cases. Specifically: (1) quantized timers were co-located with the scheduler tick and were susceptible to ~1-5ms scheduler jitter; (2) ribbon routing groups caused bursts of micro-movements between affinity buckets; (3) when these two effects combined on lightly loaded shards, the window formation code would observe no eligible items during the quantized tick and advance the timer, leaving a short void. Over time, affected tenants saw fewer formed batches, leading to apparent fairness drift. This is exacerbated by an eager fast-path that bypasses fallback aggregation when KV-cache hits are high.
repro_steps: Start a dev cluster with quantized timer wheel enabled (runtime flag: --quantized-window=enabled).
Create 3 tenant ribbons with low QPS (0.2–1 rps) and move a subset of requests across ribbons every 50ms to mimic affinity churn.
Schedule periodic CPU work on the same cores to introduce 1–6ms scheduler jitter (stress-ng tick-hog pattern).
Observe in coalescer metrics: repeated 200–800ms 'batch_formation_count' = 0 windows on some shards, and increased per-tenant request latency p99.
mitigations: Hotfix rolled at 2026-02-18 11:25 UTC: disabled ribbon-affinity fast-path for shard pool 'us-west-2-a' (rolled back the decision on experimental affinity heuristic).
Increased coalescer fallback budget to ensure at least one passive aggregation attempt per quantized interval (temporary config tweak).
Added alert for 'consecutive_zero_batch_windows > 5' per shard to catch recurrence.
action_items: ENG-981322: Replace quantized-timer delta alignment with monotonic sliding-window timers to avoid tick-synchronous misses — owner: Diego Ramirez — due: 2026-03-12
ENG-981323: Rework ribbon routing to add micro-batching stabilization (hold affinity changes for 200ms) to reduce churn — owner: Priya Nair — due: 2026-03-19
ENG-981324: Remove eager fast-path bypass that prevents fallback aggregation when KV cache hit-rate is high; ensure robust fallback path — owner: Marcus Lee — due: 2026-03-05
ENG-981325: Add deterministic integration tests that simulate scheduler jitter and verify no-zero-window behavior across shards — owner: Elena Novak — due: 2026-03-10
ENG-981326: Post-deploy canary and 48h watch with enhanced dashboards (batch formation heatmap, per-tenant window voids) — owner: SRE Team (oncall rotation) — due: 2026-03-14
follow_ups: Validate changes in canary traffic with production-like tenant distributions and low-QPS tenants included.
Run a 72-hour soak with synthetic jitter generators to ensure no regression in throughput or tail latency.
Document the timer trade-offs in the 'serving-runtime/timers' Confluence doc and add a decision record for quantized vs sliding windows.
Review potential micro-optimizations lost by disabling affinity fast-path and model their cost impact (tokens/op).
comments: 2026-02-20 — Asha Patel: Started deterministic repro in staging. Initial hypothesis: timer alignment + affinity churn. Managed to reproduce voids within 30 minutes using synthetic churn script.

2026-02-21 — Diego Ramirez: Experimented with removing quantization; switching to a micro-sliding window removed the zero-window phenomenon in the repro harness. Observed no throughput regression in 1-hour run.
2026-02-23 — Priya Nair: Ran ribbon stabilization patch in staging; affinity changes batched for 200ms. This reduced churn-related misses but did not fully eliminate voids when jitter is high.
2026-02-26 — Marcus Lee: Benchmarked fallback aggregation path changes; small CPU increase (~1.8%) but p99 latency improved for small requests.
2026-03-01 — Elena Novak: Added integration tests for scheduler jitter; tests are green locally and on CI (PR: tests#1290). Moving core runtime change to code review (PR: runtime#8342).
